precepts.text: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are. That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves; our communications must change.
precepts.point: Frederick Douglass said, it is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men. All of us come in broken, broken with sins. So in order for us to grow mentally and spiritually and improve our character: verse one, lay it all aside, then desire the sincere milk of the word.
precepts.why:
“Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” We are the temple, the spiritual house Peter speaks of. “If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves. Our communications must change. The malice, guile, hypocrisies, envies and evil speakings of 1 Peter 2:1 defile the temple.

Paul goes on in 2 Timothy: “Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation. There are brothers and sisters who are gold and silver, applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are those of wood and earth, meaning no good: fringes and a border of blue, but they have not changed their lives in two or three years. Not the new people, but those who have been with us for years and are still grimy, still that secret adulterer, still that liar, complainer, murmurer.

The captains must be able to identify in their school who is honourable and who is dishonourable. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge means cut them off, like pruning a plant and taking away the bad elements. I knew which brothers always got me in trouble; I almost got arrested many a time with those grimy brothers, and I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership. Keep the temple holy.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. I learned that very early in this truth: if they were not keeping the commandments, they could not teach me anything.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
“Every man’s work shall be made manifest”. What made Israel United in Christ different from the other organizations, some of which started building before us with far more members and resources, yet show no growth, no expansion, no change? The foundation. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”.

That was learned very early in this truth: if they weren't keeping the commandments, they couldn't teach me nothing. You would see different camps outside teaching on the Lord's Sabbath with a beanie on, scarves and head wraps, coffee steaming off the cup, telling you the white man is the damn devil and you need to join a school.

Meanwhile, how do you get to the kingdom? How do I make my marriage better, deal with my wife, deal with my kids? How can I be a better brother? What's the plan, what's the vision? None of that was being taught.

Back in 2006, when everybody was doing YouTube videos, the Bishop's videos weren't getting the hits, because they weren't the conspiracy stuff. But the good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments, and that is the foundation this body was built on.

precepts.text: Where there is no vision, the people perish. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps: talking crazy in the streets with no plan. Whose congregation is thriving with hating the black woman and hating the nations as the basis of their teaching?
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
“Where there is no vision, the people perish”. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps. In 2006 one of the biggest things taught was that 9/11 was an inside job. Israelites were doing hour-long videos on the back of the dollar bill: connect the words, it says Mason on it. There was FEMA camp doctrine, that we were all going to get killed and put in plastic coffins at Walmart. People were scared to go to Walmart. Their focus wasn't on the right thing.

Some brothers said, we're going to take to the streets and talk crazy to white folks and at the women as they walk by. Where has that gotten them today? Who grew a congregation by hating the black woman, the white man and all the other nations? Whose congregation is thriving with that as the basis of its teaching?

The Nathaniel 7 page separated many so-called teachers from those who actually feared God and understood the mission. Having a vision, a plan for our people and for the kingdom, is part of the foundation laid on Christ. Without it, the work burns and the people perish.

precepts.text: Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind. I knew I was in the right place when I was surrounded by men and women that decided to put everything behind them and do what God said, whether it was fashionable or not. At one point fringes were not fashionable; at one point modest apparel for the women was called oppression. We are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
Rather than roll with those that had no vision, the choice was to stand with those that decided to turn against the ways of the world: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

It was clear this was the right place when surrounded by men and women who decided to put everything else behind them and not be conformed to this present world, who decided, we are going to do what God said.

It may not be fashionable. At one point fringes weren't fashionable; now everybody's mama wants fringes. At one point it wasn't fashionable for women to be in a dress, fully covered in modest apparel. They said, y'all are oppressing them women. No, we are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.

That is building on the right foundation. Those who do his commandments have a good understanding, and that is why you are here as well.

precepts.text: Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock. These sayings are Christ's words: if you love me, keep my commandments. We have built this house, this congregation, on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Christ tells us how to build on him: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock”.

These sayings of mine are Christ's words. What did Christ say? If you love me, keep my commandments. What else did he say? That anybody teaching against keeping the commandments is going to be least in the kingdom of heaven.

This is what we have done here. We have built this house, this congregation, this organization on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him. We surrounded ourselves with those who decided to build on the proper foundation, and that is why this house stands.

precepts.text: Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus. Look at the back of your shirts: we built this body on the commandments of God and the faith of Christ. Is there any other way to build?
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
Look at the back of your shirts, brothers. We have built this congregation, this body, on the faith in Christ and the commandments of God: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Is there any other way to build? Can you be successful any other way? No.

That is the foundation Paul says no man can lay other than Christ. For those in the Israelite camps who want to know the secret, the secret is keeping the laws, from the beginning. As long as we stand in the spirit, the Most High God is going to bless us and you'll see the growth. When another camp asked how we set up schools in different states and countries all over the world, the answer was: we keep the commandments and faith in Christ. The Lord is not going to bring the believers to you if you haven't been sent.

precepts.text: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Go ahead and try to do it another way; a lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.
precepts.why:
Build any other way and it is going to fall. “Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.”

Go ahead and try to do it another way. A lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord. Some built their whole congregation on fear. They ran to Egypt because they thought the judgment was coming in 2012. Brothers got their passports, not to go teach but to try to deliver themselves; they left Babylon and literally led their people into a civil war, talking about safety and security. We are not built like that; this foundation is built on the rock.

Black people have the attitude that we can't build anything for ourselves and that the other nations, especially the white man, have to get involved for us to succeed. We have a totally different mindset. The Bishop always taught: make sure we have our own and never depend on anybody, because the enemy can shut you down any minute. Nobody is backing us up, and we don't need anybody to. We need each other. Together we can move mountains.

That is why we have had the success we've had: the Lord built the house. And this is just the beginning; you have not seen anything yet.

precepts.text: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? You will pull this out on a brother in the street about his tattoos, and meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy: if you are out there with the leaven in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if you both do not repent.
precepts.point: Whosoever eateth leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off from Israel: how do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps in your mind and you say, I do not like that brother; you are spiritually consuming it. That is how you get cut off from your people. This is a serious thing.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.text: Paul said, I have planted, Apollos watered, but the Most High gave the increase; Philip planted and the apostles watered, everything in order.
precepts.point: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.” That is the order here. Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, and the apostles, Peter and John, came down and watered, praying for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Everything in order, and the Most High gave the increase.

It is the same order today. The bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

moments.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Carnal, carnival and carnivore all go back to the same root, the flesh; when Paul says ye are yet carnal he means sinful, fleshly.
Carnival means raising the flesh: two days of indulging every sexual and fleshly desire, and then penance from the priest on Ash Wednesday.
The church changed the meaning to removing meat, and a folk etymology is a fake change; the word means raising the flesh, not farewell to it.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: If any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; every man's work shall be made manifest. The gold, the silver, the precious stones are the brothers that go through the fire, that go through trials, and were not destroyed. The hay and the stubble are those who, when affliction, persecution, or even offenses come, cannot endure the fire: they give up.

For the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire. That day is tribulation; when the fire comes, it tells what kind of work you are, whether you are that gold or that hay. Fire brings the impurities out of you. All of us have to go through that fire. The hay gets burnt up and leaves; the gold goes through the pain, comes out on top, and becomes stronger and better.

For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Every man's work shall be made manifest. Do you understand what this body was built on? Other organizations started building before Israel United in Christ, with far more members and far more resources, but when you look at the outcomes today, there was no growth, no expansion, no change.

Video played from the early years: why do you always talk about the commandments? All the other Israelites talk about Illuminati and curse the white man. What did God give Moses to give us? Not the Catholic religion, not Islam: all his commandments.

We have a different mindset: make sure we have our own, never depend on anybody, because the enemy can shut you down any minute. Nobody is backing us up; we do not need anybody to back us up. We need each other. For those in the Israelite camps who want to know the secret: the secret is keeping the laws. As long as we stand in the spirit, the Most High is going to bless us, and this is just the beginning.

We all go through it, but we go through it together; we push and we endure a little at a time. Some things are easier for some than for others, but if we work together it balances out, because we bear each other's burdens. If you are a one man gang, then I guess you do not need us, and I guess we do not need you.

Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire. By fire means by trial. Nobody is pouring lighter fluid on you; your trials are what reveal you. As your trials come, that is where you get your grades: how you deal with the matter, how strong you are in the spirit when things come. You lose your job and you bug out; your wife loses her job and you throw yourself out the window. Is this the first time you have ever seen poverty? We thrive in poverty; we became a nation under slavery. But you do not see it, because you think it is all about you; you are a one man nation.

Everybody has their own trials and tribulations, and they are all fit for you, custom made by the Lord to try you and your spirit, to see what you are made of. Your trial is not my trial; what comes easy for you might never come easy for me, and what comes easy for me might never come easy for you. But we are all joined together; that is 1 Corinthians 12. We all have skill sets unique to us: one officer speaks Spanish, so he goes where the Spanish is needed; another brother only has passing out flyers, but he is going on the mission, because we are going to do the Lord's work together.

And the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide, he shall receive a reward; if any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. That fire is going to burn up the work, but the man is going to be saved. A brother brought it home: a leader went through something and others bugged out, but the leader stayed in the fight. The trial was for everyone; the leader endured while others fell to the wayside. That is what this is about: endurance, going through it, enduring to the end. It might not be pretty, you might get scuffed up, but keep pushing. The Lord is not trying to kill you with this; he wants to see what you are made of.

Who is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed? I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. Paul planted by teaching people about Christ and repentance; Apollos watered by teaching them further. The teacher is the one pouring water, and he cannot pour too much or the seed corrupts.

God gives the increase, the fruit, but it is on you to study at home, cut out the thorns, and take root by believing this truth for yourself and not because of a friend. Neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth: the Most High can replace the teacher or the brother who woke you up, so nobody can be high-minded. He that planteth and he that watereth are one, and every man shall receive his own reward.
